title: The Shopping List I Forgot
scene: A quick grocery trip goes wrong when the shopping list is left at home.
sceneJa: パンを買うためにスーパーへ行ったのに、リストを忘れてチーズばかり選んでしまう。

chunks.en: I was halfway through the supermarket,
chunks.ja: スーパーを半分ほど回ったところで、

chunks.en: I'd left my shopping list at home.
chunks.ja: 買い物リストを家に忘れたことに。
引き返すこともできたけど、
なくても何とかなるだろうと。

chunks.en: I tried to go from memory,
chunks.ja: 記憶を頼りに買おうとしたけど、
なぜか買い物かごには

chunks.en: three kinds of cheese and no bread.
chunks.ja: チーズが3種類、パンはゼロ。

chunks.en: I was about to check out
chunks.ja: レジに向かおうとしたとき、
ようやく思い当たった、

chunks.en: that bread was the whole reason I'd come.
chunks.ja: そもそもパンを買いに来たのだった。
チーズを2種類棚に戻し、

chunks.en: and headed for the bakery aisle.
chunks.ja: パン売り場へ向かった。

chunks.en: By the time I got home,

questions.question: Which grouping keeps the expression together?
options: it dawned on me / that bread was the whole reason I'd come
questions.explanation: It dawned on me means I suddenly realized something.

questions.question: What does 'go from memory' mean?
questions.explanation: You rely on what you remember rather than written notes.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say 'my memory has expensive taste'?
options: They joke about buying unnecessary cheese
They are angry with the cashier
questions.explanation: It is a playful comment on an expensive mistake.

speak: In 30 seconds, tell a story about forgetting something while shopping. Explain what you tried, when it dawned on you, and how you fixed it.
review: New: go from memory（記憶を頼りに）, it dawned on me（ふと気づいた）, end up with（結果的に〜を手にする）. Review: I was about to, On second thought, By the time. Read aloud: pause before the realization; say the final line with dry humor.
